title: How the Months Remaining Are Counted in an Auto Loans Waiver Refund
content:
How the months remaining are counted, when waiver coverage financed with a loan of the Auto Loans line is closed out, turns on two readings of the borrower's Personal Checking account: whether they hold an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes, and whether at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months.

- Where both hold, the months remaining are counted from the day of the cancellation to the scheduled maturity.
- Where exactly one of those two holds, the months remaining are counted from the installment then due to the scheduled maturity.
- Where neither of them holds, the months remaining are the term less the whole months since funding.

## The three counts on one loan

Take a loan written for 60 months, funded 18 whole months ago, whose scheduled maturity falls 41 whole months after the day of the cancellation and 42 whole months after the date the installment then due falls on. Under the first count the months remaining are 41; under the second, 42; under the third, 60 less 18, which is 42.

The three counts can agree by chance on one loan and part company on another, since two of them run from a date and the third from the term.

## What the two readings compare

The balance reading compares the posted balance on the borrower's active account in the Personal Checking line against the fee-waiver daily balance published for that account's tier. The deposit reading counts recurring deposits posted to that same account over the three months ending on the day of the cancellation; exactly 2 meets the reading and 1 does not.
